source.note: Seed idea reconstructed from a prior AAVA Product Studio PRD rather than a fresh free-text brief; treated as raw input to re-run through the pipeline.

problem_statement: Executives and corporate legal/compliance teams at publicly traded companies using Computershare's EquatePlus platform rely on manual, error-prone processes to file securities transaction disclosures (starting with SEC Form 4). SEC Form 4 must be filed within 2 business days of a trade; the current manual process only achieves ~70% on-time, error-free filing, exposing individuals and the company to financial penalties, legal consequences, and reputational harm.

target_users.definition: Insider subject to SEC/regulatory reporting obligations after executing a securities transaction.
target_users.primary_need: Get a compliant filing done fast, with minimal manual effort and clear visibility into status/deadlines.

target_users.definition: Corporate legal/compliance department staff who review, edit, approve, and submit regulatory filings on behalf of executives.
target_users.primary_need: Real-time visibility across all executives' filings, low-friction review/approval, and a defensible audit trail.

candidate_success_metrics: % of regulatory filings submitted within required deadline, error-free (baseline 70%, target 98%)
Average time from transaction execution to form submission (baseline 24h, target 30min)
Manual data-entry errors per month (baseline 5, target 0)
candidate_success_metrics_provenance: Baselines (70% on-time rate, 24h avg time-to-file, 5 errors/month) are carried forward as-stated from PRD.txt section 8 (Success Metrics & KPIs), which itself does not cite an underlying data source or system of record. Treat as unverified planning inputs, not confirmed measurements, until Legal & Compliance can confirm them against an actual EquatePlus/compliance incident log. Flagged per gr-L1-citation-verifier during Phase 0 quality review.
known_constraints: Integration limited to EquatePlus platform APIs only
Must align authentication with existing corporate SSO
US regulatory forms only at launch (SEC Form 4); no non-US jurisdictions
No manual transaction entry in scope
